title: Turn Clusterer: memory-aware stream batch formation for low-jitter chat completions
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a "turn clusterer" that forms streaming-chat micro-batches by jointly reasoning about turn timing, request token budgets, KV cache footprint, and GPU slab availability. Goal: reduce tail latency jitter for streaming completions while keeping per-token cost within targets and avoiding OOMs under mixed-priority workloads.
acceptance_criteria: New batcher composes micro-batches with <=10% increase in average per-token cost compared to baseline while reducing 95th percentile generation latency by >=15% for streaming workloads
No increase in GPU OOM incidents in staging for representative mixes (normal+priority+long-context) over a 48h run
KV cache resident size per GPU remains within configured slab reservation thresholds (±5%) during peak simulated traffic
Can be toggled via runtime feature flag and rolled back without disrupting in-flight streams
Observability: per-batch metadata (reason for grouping, token estimate, slab reservation id, predicted kv-entries) emitted to console traces and dashboards
implementation_notes: Batch formation inputs: time-since-last-token (turn age), expected remaining tokens (based on prompt and model profile), conversation priority tag, kv-cache keycard size (MB), GPU slab free bytes, and router affinity hints

Core algorithm: lightweight greedy clustering with tiered heuristics: first apply priority pinning, then affinity (same convo or same tenant), then memory-fit packing using First-Fit-Decreasing on estimated token*KvMultiplier to respect slab reservations

Introduce two thresholds: soft_hold_ms (small delay to allow immediate sibling turns to join) and hard_cut_ms (max buffering before flush). Default soft_hold_ms=20ms, hard_cut_ms=150ms; expose via config and per-model overrides

KV prefetch hint: when a cluster includes turns with partially overlapping contexts, prefetch union of KV slots and mark entries with a 'merge-safe' flag allowing partial eviction if memory pressure occurs
Graceful degradation: if slab pressure exceeds reserve_ratio (configurable), automatically shrink micro-batches (aggressive single-turn mode) and surface metric + trace that rollback happened
Backpressure signals: when long-tail sessions with huge KV footprint are present, emit Router-level signals to route new low-priority sessions to dedicated pools or rate-limit
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Unit tests + integration tests for estimator (token estimator, kv size estimator), run in CI (2 days)
Phase 1: Canary on low-traffic shard with feature-flag (10% traffic) for 24h, collect latency/cost/kv-metrics
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 50% over 72h if no OOM/regression, enable slab reservation telemetry
Phase 3: Full rollout with automatic fallback to legacy batcher on detecting slab breach or increased error rate
Experimentation: A/B test variant that uses entropy-based clustering (score conversation entropy and prefer similar-entropy grouping) to evaluate quality impact
